title: feat(types,permissions)!: retire PermissionGuardConfig from both published surfaces (objectui#8024)
body:
Fixes #8024
Clause-②: yes — a published type export (`PermissionGuardConfig`) is removed from `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/permissions` (ruling 5809899168).

## What

Executes the maintainer ruling on this card (UI closure batch 4 item 3, letter **remove**): `PermissionGuardConfig` leaves both published surfaces.

- `packages/types/src/permissions.ts` — the `export interface PermissionGuardConfig` declaration is replaced by a `//` RETIRED note at the old site. The note names **`PermissionGuardProps`** (`packages/permissions/src/PermissionGuard.tsx`) as the shape the shipped guard reads, and states that `fallback: 'redirect'` / `redirectPath` **never existed** as a capability. It does not say "not yet supported", and it adds no config-driven branch and no redirect.
- `packages/types/src/index.ts` and `packages/permissions/src/index.ts` — only the `PermissionGuardConfig` re-export line changes in each. It becomes a `//` pointer to the note.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/permission-guard-config-retired-8024.test.ts` — the retirement pin, described below.
- `.changeset/8024-retire-permission-guard-config.md` — `'@object-ui/types': minor` and `'@object-ui/permissions': minor`, with a **BREAKING** body that names the removed export and `PermissionGuardProps`. No `major`.

**Tombstone form: the whole-type-name precedent.** The retire-vs-remove discriminator is stated on `ChatbotSchema` / `KanbanColumn.color` in `complex.ts`, in the form objectui#7678 amended it to. A `?: never` tombstone needs a surviving carrier, and a whole exported type name has none, so the name is removed outright. The note is copied from the objectui#7519 retirement of `MobileResponsiveConfig` / `GestureConfig` in `mobile.ts`, which was the same case: a declaration plus two barrel re-exports and nothing else. The note is a `//` comment, so declaration emit leaves it out of `dist/*.d.ts`. The note cites the rule and does not restate it, so `tombstone-discriminator-agreement-9684.test.ts` stays green.

## Premise re-measured (the card's zones)

- **H0: `@objectstack/spec` has no such shape.** It was measured in two places.
  - The installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, which `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins, has zero files anywhere in the package containing `PermissionGuardConfig`, `PermissionGuard`, `redirectPath` or `fallbackComponent`. Lit control: `PermissionSetSchema` is in 46 files. No `'hide', 'disable'` enum exists in `src`. The only `fallback` enum is `fallback: z.enum(['404', 'proxy', 'custom'])` in `src/api/dispatcher.zod.ts`, which is HTTP dispatcher routing and not a guard.
  - objectstack `origin/main` `a08e059`: `git grep` over `packages/spec` finds none of the four names (exit 1), while `PermissionSetSchema` is found in 24 files (exit 0). Over the whole objectstack tree the four names are also absent (exit 1).
  - ⇒ The retirement is one leg. It is not re-scoped.
- **H1: nothing read it.** Base `1daf4773f`, full tree:
  - `PermissionGuardConfig` has 3 hits: the declaration and the two re-exports.
  - `redirectPath` and `fallbackComponent` have 1 hit each, their own declaration lines.
  - Control: `PermissionGuardProps` has 3 hits.
  - Full history, after unshallowing: pickaxe `-S"'redirect'"` over `packages/permissions/` finds **0 commits**. Pickaxe `-S redirectPath` over `packages/` finds only `954168aaf`, the commit that added the declaration. Control: pickaxe `-S fallbackContent` finds `49ddc8b6a`, the package's creation.
  - ⇒ "never existed" holds over the full history. It is not only true today.
- **H3: ledgers.** No ledger moved.
  - `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts` counts declarations, and this name had exactly one. It is green.
  - No test or census enumerates this name.
  - `check:readme-exports`: neither README names the type.
- **H5: pending changesets.** `git grep -l PermissionGuardConfig -- .changeset/` finds nothing (exit 1). The control `PermissionContext` is found (exit 0). Nothing needed reconciling.

## Red on base, green on head (the pin)

Run from the committed head `efdc3e3fe`. The three source files were reverted to base `1daf4773f` inside a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` script. The pin was left in place.

- Checked on disk after the revert: `decl=1 typesReexport=1 permReexport=1 note=0`.
- **RED:**
  - `vitest`: `Tests  3 failed | 3 passed (6)`. The three failures are both barrel legs and the declaring-file note leg.
  - `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json`: `error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.` on both directive lines of the pin.
- **Restore proof:** `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status` is clean. The `hash-object` result equals `rev-parse HEAD:path` for all three paths (`MATCH` ×3).
- **GREEN on head:**
  - `vitest run packages/types/ packages/permissions/ scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts`: `Test Files  247 passed (247)`, `Tests  5363 passed (5363)`.
  - The pin alone: 6/6.
  - `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the pin, with 0 errors.

| `type-check` for `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/permissions` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` (types runs `tsc --noEmit`, examples and test projects; permissions runs `tsc --noEmit` and the test project) |

The `--list` rows for both READMEs are all `real` (36) plus one `local-declaration`, with 0 fabricated. The full run exits 1 on the collapse floor because 34 other packages are unbuilt. Their export surfaces are byte-unchanged by this diff: no package star-re-exports `@object-ui/types` or `@object-ui/permissions` (0 hits, while the control star-export pattern has 324), and the name had no other re-export site. CI runs the full gate after `turbo build ./packages/*` |

Consumer sweep: the tree was checked for the name's absence instead of rebuilding the consumer closure. On head, every remaining mention of `PermissionGuardConfig` is in backticked prose: the note, two barrel pointers, the pin and the changeset.

## Acceptance notes

- `PermissionGuard` itself has no production mount in this tree. Its only call sites are the two README examples. This is an observation, not a finding.
- The `'disable'` arm of `PermissionGuard` renders an inline `style` with opacity and pointer-events. That is outside this card, and I left it alone.
- The `permissions.ts` module header still reads "aligned with @objectstack/spec v2.0.1". That is stale prose, and I left it alone.
- I unshallowed this worktree's object store (`git fetch --unshallow origin main`) so the pickaxe could run over the full history.
